extraction_text: A charioteer named Adhiratha and his wife Radha found a floating basket containing a baby in the Ganges River.

attributes.relationships: Adhiratha and Radha adopt the baby as their son, naming him Karna (also called Vrisha).
attributes.supernatural_elements: The baby is described as divine-looking, wearing golden armor and earrings, suggesting celestial origin.

extraction_text: Radha raised Karna with proper rites, and he grew strong and valiant. Later, Radha also gave birth to her own sons.

attributes.relationships: Karna is raised as the eldest son in the family.

extraction_text: Karna, wearing divine armor and earrings, was given the name Vrisha by Brahmins and became known as a mighty prince raised as a charioteer's son.

attributes.relationships: Karna is acknowledged as a prince despite his charioteer upbringing.

extraction_text: Spies of Pritha (Kunti) discovered Karna wearing divine armor.

attributes.relationships: Kunti's spies identify Karna, hinting at a hidden connection.

extraction_text: Adhiratha sent the grown-up Karna to Hastinapura, where he learned martial arts from Drona, became friends with Duryodhana, and mastered four martial arts from Drona, Kripa, and Rama, becoming a renowned archer.

attributes.relationships: Karna becomes a student of Drona and a close ally of Duryodhana, forming a friendship and martial bond.

extraction_text: Karna allied with Duryodhana and harbored hatred for the sons of Pritha (the Pandavas), always eager to fight Arjuna.

attributes.relationships: Karna becomes a rival to the Pandavas, particularly Arjuna, strengthening his alliance with Duryodhana.

extraction_text: Yudhishthira, seeing Karna's earrings and armor, worried that Karna could not be killed in battle.

attributes.relationships: Yudhishthira perceives Karna as a formidable threat to the Pandavas.

extraction_text: Indra, disguised as a Brahmin, approached Karna during his noon prayers to the sun to beg for alms, knowing Karna never refused any request at that time.

attributes.relationships: Indra tests or seeks to exploit Karna's generosity.
attributes.supernatural_elements: Indra transforms into a Brahmin as part of a divine plan.

extraction_text: Karna offered the Brahmin a golden-necked woman or a village full of cattle.
The Brahmin refused Karna's initial offers and demanded Karna's innate armor and earrings instead.

attributes.reason: The Brahmin seeks Karna's divine armor and earrings, considering them the highest gain.

extraction_text: Karna refused to give his armor and earrings, offering other gifts like land, women, cattle, and years of provisions instead.

attributes.reason: Karna states the armor and earrings are born from nectar and make him invincible; giving them up would leave him vulnerable to enemies.

extraction_text: The Brahmin persisted in demanding only the armor and earrings, rejecting all other offers.
Karna revealed he recognized the Brahmin as Indra, the king of gods, and proposed a conditional exchange.

attributes.condition: Karna demands something in return to avoid being killed and Indra being ridiculed.

extraction_text: Indra confirmed his identity and offered Karna any boon except his thunderbolt (vajra).
Karna chose Indra's infallible spear (shakti) that kills hundreds of enemies and returns to the thrower, in exchange for his armor and earrings.

attributes.items_exchanged: Karna's armor and earrings for Indra's infallible spear
attributes.supernatural_element: The spear is a divine weapon with magical properties.

extraction_text: Indra agreed to the exchange, taking Karna's armor and earrings and giving him the spear.

attributes.outcome: Karna gains a powerful weapon but loses his invincibility, making him vulnerable in future battles.

extraction_text: Indra offered Karna a magical spear that could kill only one powerful, roaring, shining enemy and then return.

attributes.condition: Spear can kill only one specific enemy then returns

extraction_text: Karna stated he wanted to kill only one roaring, shining enemy in battle, possibly out of fear.
Indra revealed that Karna's intended target is protected by Krishna, who is known by various divine names.
Karna agreed to give his divine earrings and armor to Indra in exchange for the spear.

attributes.exchange: Divine armor and earrings for magical spear
attributes.condition: Karna asks not to feel fear during cutting

extraction_text: Indra assured Karna he wouldn't feel fear or leave scars, and would retain his father's complexion and radiance.

attributes.assurance: No fear, no scars, retains appearance
attributes.warning: Spear will turn against Karna if used carelessly

extraction_text: Karna vowed to use the spear only in greatest danger and accepted it from Indra.

attributes.vow: Use spear only in extreme danger

extraction_text: Karna cut off his divine armor and earrings with a knife, showing no pain and even smiling.

attributes.supernatural: No pain, celestial music, flower rain
attributes.new_name: Karna becomes known as Vrikodara (the cutter)

extraction_text: Indra took the bloodied armor and earrings, smiling at his successful deception, then returned to heaven.
The Kaurava princes became dejected upon learning of Karna's deception, while the Pandavas in the forest rejoiced.
Janamejaya asked where the Pandavas were living and what they were doing after twelve years of exile.
Vaishampayana described how the Pandavas, after defeating Sindhu King and rescuing Draupadi, returned to Kamyaka forest.
The Pandavas completed their difficult forest life and returned to the sacred Dvaita forest.
